title: Remarks at Riceville, Tennessee
checks: Day by Day, which follows the Theodore Roosevelt Association's Chronological Record, places him at Sagamore Hill on this date, about 1,150 km from Riceville. One of the two dates may be wrong.
paragraphs: I am glad to have the chance of saying a word of greeting to you. I am thoroughly enjoying my trip through Eastern Tennessee. I came down here to attend the meeting of the brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen, but in addition to that it is a particular pleasure to come here in the battle valley of the Tennessee, in which the state took its rise-into which the pioneers came even before the Revolutionary War; and I spent most of yesterday going over the Battlefields of Chickamauga and Chattanooga, Missionary Ridge and Lookout Mountain. I don't see how any halfway decent American can come away not feeling better than before. I am very glad to see you, my fellow countrymen. (Applause)
